newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates steady in slower trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates steady in slower trade.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were stable in modest trade on Tuesday amid improved bank liquidity ahead of the monthly pension pay date, dealers said.

"The banks' accounts have risen to 399 million kuna from Saturday's 284 million," one dealer told Reuters, adding the improvement was due in part to the Pension Fund filling accounts ahead of the monthly payout.
New deals amounted to 11 million kuna, of which 9.5 million was call money granted at a steady 10.5 percent rate.
One previously arranged call money loan was made at 12.5 percent and a 1.5 million kuna one-week interbank loan at 11 percent.
Some 15 million kuna were left on the supply and six million on the demand side, but lenders and borrowers could not agree on terms.
Monday's overnight trade totalled 30 million kuna, which three banks used to maintain their mandatory reserves. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
